title: Nim with Three Piles
statement: Two players take turns removing any positive number of stones from a single pile. The player who takes the last stone wins. The piles start at $3$, $5$ and $7$ stones. How many different first moves guarantee a win for the first player?
insight: A position is losing for the player to move exactly when the XOR (nim-sum) of the pile sizes is 0. 3 ⊕ 5 ⊕ 7 = 1, and a winning move is any move that makes the XOR 0.
redHerring: Trying to search the game tree by hand.
hints: Find a quantity that is 0 at the end and that every move from 0 makes nonzero.
Write the pile sizes in binary and XOR them.
A move on pile $p$ wins iff it changes $p$ to $p \oplus s$, where $s$ is the current nim-sum. For which piles is that smaller than $p$?
solution:
By Bouton's theorem, the player to move loses iff the nim-sum (XOR) of the piles is $0$. Here $3\oplus5\oplus7 = 1$.

A winning move turns some pile $p$ into $p\oplus1$, which is possible iff $p\oplus1<p$, i.e. $p$ is odd. All three piles are odd: $3\to2$, $5\to4$, $7\to6$. That's $3$ winning moves.
